  CITY COUNCIL OF MONTEREY PARK

  April 6, 2022
  6:30 p.m.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services
  to enhance the quality of life for our entire community.

GENERAL INFORMATION
Documents related to an Agenda item are available to the public in the City Clerk’s Office located at 320
West Newmark Avenue, Monterey Park, CA 91754, during normal business hours and the City’s website
at http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/AgendaCenter/City-Council-17.

The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99
or Charter Communications, channel 182) or by visiting the city’s website at
http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
You may speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. You may combine up to 2 minutes of time with another
person’s speaking. No person may speak more than a total of 10 minutes. The Mayor and City Council
may change the amount of time allowed for speakers.

Per the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting,
please call City Hall at (626) 307-1359 for reasonable accommodation at least 24 hours before a meeting.
Council Chambers are wheelchair accessible.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS:
While all comments are welcome, the Brown Act does not allow the City Council to take action on any
item not on the agenda. The Council may briefly respond to comments after Public Communications is
closed. Persons may, in addition to any other matter within the City Council's subject-matter jurisdiction,
comment on Agenda Items at this time. If you provide public comment on a specific Agenda item at this
time, however, you cannot later provide comments at the time the Agenda Item is considered.

  • Fire Department

  • Public Works Department

  It is recommended that the City Council consider:

  (2)  Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.
   Monterey Park City Council Agenda, April 6, 2022 - Page 3

3-D.  2020-2021 ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT

3-E.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AMENDMENT WITH BARTEL ASSOCIATES, LLC FOR THE

ADJOURN

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  FINANCING AUTHORITY (MPFA)
  HOUSING AUTHORITY (MPHA)
  GEOLOGIC HAZARD ABATEMENT DISTRICT (GHAD)
  SUCCESSOR AGENCY (SA)
  REGULAR MEETING
  APRIL 6, 2022

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the
City of Monterey Park held a Regular Meeting of the Council in the Council Chamber,
located at 320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, April
6, 2020 at 6:30 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Lo called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE:
The Monterey Park Fire Explorers

ROLL CALL:
City Clerk Vincent Chang called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Peter Chan, Hans Liang, Henry Lo, Yvonne Yiu
Council Members Absent:  Fred Sornoso

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Ron Bow, Assistant City Manager Inez Alvarez, Fire
Chief Matt Hallock, Police Chief Kelly Gordon, Director of Management Services Martha
Garcia, Director of Recreation & Community Services Robert Aguirre, Public Works
Manager Chris Reyes, Firefighter Scott Kelley, Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang, Assistant
Deputy City Clerk Helena Cho, Community Communications Coordinator Randy Ishino

VIRTUALLY PRESENT: City Treasurer Jospeh Leon, City Attorney Karl Berger, City
Librarian Diana Garcia, Interim Director of Community & Economic Development Steve
Sizemore, Interim Director of Public Works Anthony Antich

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS – None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

  - Sarkis Antonian voiced his opinion on the expansion of Garvey Avenue and the
  construction of a parking structure on Garvey Avenue. He also inquired about the
  vote by mail drop boxes located throughout the City.

  MISSION STATEMENT
  The mission of the City of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community
   70-62
  April 6, 2022
  - Nancy Acuri inquired about the Measure R funding being used to expand Garvey
  Avenue during rush hour traffic.

  - Scott Kwong communicated that Council should reconsider adding bike lanes to
  Monterey Pass Road and the lane expansion of Garvey Avenue.

  - John Wong voiced his opposition to adding bike lanes to Monterey Pass Road
  and expanding the lanes on Garvey Avenue.

  - Jennifer Tang, on behalf of 49th District Assemblymember Mike Fong,
  encouraged residents to contact Assemblymember Fong’s office regarding any
  concerns on upcoming bills or state related matters. She also announced that
  Assemblymember Fong is looking forward to working with City staff and the City
  Council.

  - City Clerk Chang received, filed, and read into the record a written
  communication from Ming Lai regarding parking concerns on Fremont Avenue
  and Monterey Pass Road.

  - City Clerk Chang read into the record a letter received on March 29, 2022 from
  Mayor Pro Tem Fred Sornoso regarding his resignation from City Council due to
  health concerns, effective April 14, 2022.

STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

  - Firefighter Kelley invited the community to attend Fire Service Day on May 14th,
  2022 at Fire Station 62.

  - Director of Recreation & Community Services Aguirre reminded the community of
  the MPK Spring Hunt at the Barnes Park Field on April 14, 2022.

  - Public Works Manager Chris Reyes informed the community of the Spring
  Cleaning event on April 9, 2022 at the Barnes Park Service Club House.

1.  PRESENTATION – None.

  Matters listed under presentation are for informational content and discussion only.

2.  OLD BUSINESS

2A. AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT FUNDING

  On March 11, 2021, President Joseph R. Biden signed into law the American
  Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) of 2021, a $1.9 trillion federal aid package designed to
  help the American people and American economy recover from the prolonged
  impacts felt from COVID-19. The bill includes $350 billion in direct financial relief
   70-63
  April 6, 2022
  for all state, local, tribal, and territorial governments known as the Coronavirus
  State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) $15,043,184 of which has been
  allocated to the City of Monterey Park.

  The City received half of its allocation ($7,521,592) in June 2021 with the
  remaining amount to be received in June 2022. City Council has approved
  appropriations of $6,925,837 million to be expensed on allowable purchases.

  The City is requesting direction for the remaining ARPA funds.

  Recommendation: It is recommended that City Council (1) reviewing, discussing,
  and providing direction on the allocation of American Rescue Plan Act funding; and
  (2) taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

  Action Taken: Mayor Lo and Council Member Chan declared a potential property-
  related conflict of interest as their properties are within 1000 feet of items related to
  Garvey Ranch Park. They did not participate in discussion on items relating to
  Garvey Ranch Park. The City Council received and filed the American Rescue
  Plan Act Funding report.

3.  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS NOS. 3A-3F
  Matters listed under consent calendar are considered to be routine, ongoing
  business and are enacted by one motion unless specified.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved and adopted Item Nos. 3A, 3B, 3E, and
  3F, on Consent Calendar, excluding Item Nos. 3C and 3D which were pulled for
  discussion and separate motion, reading resolutions and ordinances by the title
  only and waiving further reading thereof.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Liang and seconded by Council Member Yiu,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Yiu, Chan, Liang, Lo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  Sornoso
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

3A. MINUTES

  Approving the minutes from the regular meeting of March 2, 2022.

  Action Taken: The City Council approved the minutes from the regular meeting of
  March 2, 2022 on Consent Calendar.
   70-64
  April 6, 2022
3B. WAIVE FURTHER READING AND ADOPT AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING
  THE LAND USE RELATED TIME SUSPENSION PERIOD RELATED TO THE
  COVID-19 EMERGENCY

  The Ordinance was introduced and received first reading at the March 16, 2022
  City Council meeting. The original staff report, from March 16, 2022, is attached to
  the staff report for reference. Second reading and adoption of this Ordinance is
  recommended. If adopted, the Ordinance will take effect in 30 days.

  Action Taken: The City Council waived the second reading and adopted
  Ordinance No. 2219 on Consent Calendar.

  Ordinance No. 2219:
  AN UNCODIFIED ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE LAND USE RELATED
  TIME SUSPENSION PERIOD RELATED TO THE COVID-19 EMERGENCY

3C. WAIVE FURTHER READING AND ADOPT AN ORDINANCE AMENDING
  VARIOUS SECTIONS OF MONTEREY PARK MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER
  6.15 REGULATING MANDATORY ORGANIC WASTE DISPOSAL REDUCTION

  The Ordinance was introduced and received first reading at the March 16, 2022
  City Council meeting. The original staff report, from March 16, 2022, is attached to
  the staff report for reference. Second reading and adoption of this Ordinance is
  recommended. If adopted, the Ordinance will take effect in 30 days.

  Public Communications:

  - Nancy Acuri voiced her concerns regarding using the green bin disposal for
  green waste and food waste.

  Action Taken: The City Council waived the second reading and adopted
  Ordinance No. 2220.

  Motion: Moved by Council Member Chan and seconded by Council Member Yiu,
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Yiu, Chan, Liang, Lo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  Sornoso
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

  Ordinance No. 2220:
  AN ORDINANCE AMENDING VARIOUS SECTIONS OF MONTEREY PARK
  MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 6.15 REGULATING MANDATORY ORGANIC
  WASTE DISPOSAL REDUCTION
   70-65
  April 6, 2022
3D. 2020-2021 ANNUAL COMPREHENSIVE FINANCIAL REPORT (ACFR)

  The City’s auditor, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP (CLA), an independent auditor and one
  of the nation’s leading CPA firms, completed the audit of the City’s annual financial
  statements for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2021. The audited financial
  statements are incorporated into an ACFR.

  This is the 6th year, CLA audited the City’s financial records. The auditor issued an
  unmodified (“clean”) opinion on the City’s financial statements. An unmodified
  opinion indicates that the financial data of the City is fairly presented in accordance
  with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (or
  “GAAP”) and the standards applicable to the financial audits contained in
  Government Audit Standards, issued by the Comptroller General of the United
  States. These standards require that the auditors plan and perform the audit to
  obtain reasonable assurance as to whether the financial statements are free of
  material misstatement and accurately reflects the City’s financial position.
  Additionally, the auditors’ report does not indicate any negative findings, internal
  control deficiencies or instances of noncompliance with applicable laws and
  regulations.

  Action Taken: The City Council received and filed the City’s 2020-2021 Annual
  Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) on Consent Calendar.

3E. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AMENDMENT WITH BARTEL ASSOCIATES, LLC
  FOR THE CALPERS RETIREMENT PLAN, EMPOWER RETIREMENT PLAN,
  AND OTHER POSTEMPLOYMENT BENEFITS ACTUARIAL VALUATION
  PROPOSALS AND DATA REQUESTS

  On September 2, 2020, City Council authorized a professional services agreement
  with Bartel Associates, LLC for the purpose of CalPERS Retirement Plan pension
  override tax study, actuarial valuation proposals and data request. Continued work
  with Bartel Associates LLC is desirable to assist with on other actuarial valuation
  proposals and data requests including the CalPERS Retirement Plan, Empower
  Retirement Plan, and OPEB. Accordingly, it is requested that the City Council
  authorize the City Manager to execute an Amendment for a total amount of
  $135,800.

  Public Communications:

  - Mary Beth Redding, Bartel Associate, was available virtually to answer any
  questions.
   70-66
  April 6, 2022
  Action Taken: The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute an
  Amendment with Bartel Associates, LLC in a form approved by the City Attorney,
  to provide CalPERS Retirement Plan, Empower Retirement Plan, and Other
  Postemployment Benefits (OPEB) actuarial valuation proposals and data requests
  for an amount of $135,800 on Consent Calendar.

3F. STATE HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM SUBRECIPIENT AGREEMENT
  GRANT YEAR 2020 – AWARD OF AGREEMENT

  The County of Los Angeles is a Subgrantee of the State Homeland Security
  Program Grant Year 2020 ("SHSP 2020") that is provided by the U.S. Department
  of Homeland Security. Per the subrecipient agreement, the County of Los Angeles
  is authorized to enter into a subrecipient agreement with the City of Monterey Park,
  which includes a distribution of SHSP 2020 grant funds to the City of Monterey
  Park in the amount of $182,720. A portion of the $182,720 is dedicated to fund a
  fulltime Regional Training (RïG) lntelligence Chief position for the Los Angeles
  Area Fire Chiefs Association (LAAFCA). Upon approval of the subrecipient
  agreement, staff will publicize a Request for Proposal, to fill the position by July
  1,2022, and oversee administration of funds for this position. Staff recommends
  City Council to authorize the City to execute an agreement, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney, with the County of Los Angeles for an amount not to exceed
  5182,720 for the SHSP 2020 Grant.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R18 authorizing the
  City Manager to apply for, receive, and execute an agreement, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney, with the County of Los Angeles for an amount not to exceed
  $182,720, for the State Homeland Security Program Grant Year 2020 on Consent
  Calendar.

  Resolution No. 2022-R18:
  A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER, OR DESIGNEE, TO
  APPLY FOR, RECEIVE, AND APPROPRIATE GRANT FUNDS FOR THE STATE
  HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM FOR GRANT YEAR 2020

4.  PUBLIC HEARING – None.

5.  NEW BUSINESS – None.
   70-67
  April 6, 2022

6.  CITY COMMUNICATIONS (CITY COUNCIL)

6A. A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK
  ENSURING EQUAL POLICIES FOR REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH CARE
  SERVICES (Requested by Mayor Henry Lo and Councilmember Yvonne Yiu)

  Written Communications:

  - City Clerk Chang received, filed, and read into the record three written
  communications from Jeff Schwartz, on behalf of the Monterey Park Democratic
  Club and the California Democratic Party, Linda Tang, and Je-Show Yang
  voicing their support for Agenda Item 6A and urging City Council to vote yes.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2022-R19 ensuring equal
  policies for reproductive healthcare services.

  Motion: Moved by Mayor Lo and seconded by Council Member Yiu, motion carried
  by the following vote:

  Ayes:  Council Members:  Yiu, Chan, Liang, Lo
  Noes:  Council Members:  None
  Absent:  Council Members:  Sornoso
  Abstain:  Council Members:  None

  Resolution No. 2022-R19:
  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MONTEREY PARK
  ENSURING EQUAL POLICIES FOR REPRODUCTIVE HEALTHCARE
  SERVICES

Council Communications:

  Council Member Yiu expressed her excitement to be back to in person meetings in
  the Council Chambers.

  Council Member Chan stated that it is good to be back to in person meetings in the
  Council Chambers and reminded the community to continue to stay safe. He
  reported that he attended the grand opening of the Chinatown Service Center’s
  new office on Atlantic Blvd, the Japanese Consul General’s residence to celebrate
  the Emperor’s birthday, and the International Cities Association (ICA) conference.

  Council Member Liang announced that he is happy to be back to in person
  meeting in the Council Chambers and wished Mayor Pro Tem Fred Sornoso all the
  best.
   70-68
  April 6, 2022

  Mayor Lo reported that he is happy to be back to holding in person meetings in the
  Council Chambers and thanked the public for attending the meeting. He also
  voiced appreciation for Mayor Pro Tem Sornoso for serving on City Council.

7.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
  None.

8.  CLOSED SESSION (IF REQUIRED; CITY ATTORNEY TO ANNOUNCE)
  None.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business for consideration, the meeting was adjourned at 8:11
p.m.

Vincent D. Chang
City Clerk
